Type in the box to filter. Each entry links to the module section where the term is explained. Quarto's search (top right) searches the full text of every page.

```{=html}
<input id="gl-filter" type="search" class="form-control" placeholder="Filter terms, e.g. R-hat, shrinkage, LOO …" style="max-width:420px;margin:0.5rem 0 1.5rem;">
<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
  var input = document.getElementById('gl-filter');
  input.addEventListener('input', function () {
    var q = input.value.toLowerCase().trim();
    document.querySelectorAll('.glossary dt').forEach(function (dt) {
      var dd = dt.nextElementSibling;
      var text = (dt.textContent + ' ' + (dd ? dd.textContent : '')).toLowerCase();
      var show = !q || text.indexOf(q) !== -1;
      dt.style.display = show ? '' : 'none';
      if (dd) dd.style.display = show ? '' : 'none';
    });
    document.querySelectorAll('.glossary h2').forEach(function (h) {
      var dl = h.parentNode.querySelector('dl');
      if (!dl) return;
      var any = Array.from(dl.querySelectorAll('dt')).some(function (dt) { return dt.style.display !== 'none'; });
      h.style.display = any ? '' : 'none';
    });
  });
});
</script>
```

::: {.glossary}

## A–C

Adapt delta (`adapt_delta`)
: Stan's target acceptance rate during warm-up (default 0.8). Raising it (0.95, 0.99) gives smaller steps and fewer divergent transitions, at the cost of speed. [M3 §3.7](module3.qmd#t3-7)

AIC
: Akaike information criterion: −2 × log-likelihood at the maximum + 2 × number of parameters. Ignores posterior uncertainty. [M4 §4.7](module4.qmd#t4-7)

Autocorrelation
: Correlation between MCMC draws a given number of iterations apart. High autocorrelation lowers the effective sample size. [M3 §3.10](module3.qmd#t3-10)

Base-rate fallacy
: Ignoring the prior probability (prevalence) when interpreting evidence, e.g. reading sensitivity as the positive predictive value. [M1 §1.3](module1.qmd#t1-3)

Bayes factor
: Ratio of the marginal likelihoods of two models; turns prior odds into posterior odds. Depends on the priors inside each model. [M1 §1.9](module1.qmd#t1-9)

Bayes' rule
: $p(\theta \mid y) = p(y \mid \theta)\,p(\theta) / p(y)$. [M1 §1.3](module1.qmd#t1-3)

Bayesian model averaging (pseudo-BMA)
: Averaging predictive distributions with weights proportional to $\exp(-\tfrac12 \text{WAIC})$ or the LOO equivalent. [M4 §4.10](module4.qmd#t4-10)

Beta–Binomial
: The conjugate pair Beta prior + binomial likelihood (posterior Beta(a + y, b + n − y)), and the posterior predictive distribution of a new count. [M2 §2.6](module2.qmd#t2-6) · [§2.9](module2.qmd#t2-9)

Bias–variance trade-off
: MSE = bias² + variance. Shrinkage accepts some bias for a larger drop in variance. [M5 §5.9](module5.qmd#t5-9)

brms
: R package that turns an lme4-style formula into a Stan program and fits it with NUTS. [M3 §3.11](module3.qmd#t3-11)

Burn-in / warm-up
: Initial MCMC iterations that are discarded. In Stan, warm-up also tunes the sampler. [M3 §3.4](module3.qmd#t3-4) · [§3.7](module3.qmd#t3-7)

Calibration
: Frequentist properties (bias, coverage) of a Bayesian procedure, studied by simulation. [M6 §6.6](module6.qmd#t6-6)

Complete pooling
: All groups assumed identical; one common parameter. [M5 §5.2](module5.qmd#t5-2)

Confidence interval
: An interval from a procedure that covers the true value in a stated share of hypothetical repetitions. Not a probability statement about the parameter. [M1 §1.8](module1.qmd#t1-8)

Conjugate prior
: A prior whose posterior belongs to the same family, so updating is arithmetic on its parameters. [M2 §2.6](module2.qmd#t2-6)

Coverage
: The share of intervals that contain the true value over repeated experiments. [M2 §2.8](module2.qmd#t2-8)

Credible interval
: An interval containing the parameter with a stated posterior probability, given model, prior and data. Equal-tailed or HPD. [M1 §1.5](module1.qmd#t1-5)

Crossed random effects
: Grouping factors that are not nested, e.g. region and survey round. [M5 §5.7](module5.qmd#t5-7)

## D–K

DIC
: Deviance information criterion: posterior mean deviance plus a penalty from the posterior variance of the deviance. [M4 §4.7](module4.qmd#t4-7)

Divergent transition
: An HMC trajectory that broke down in a region of high curvature; a sign the draws may be biased. [M3 §3.7](module3.qmd#t3-7)

Effective sample size (ESS; bulk and tail)
: The number of independent draws with the same information as the autocorrelated MCMC draws. Bulk for means and SDs, tail for interval limits. [M3 §3.10](module3.qmd#t3-10)

elpd
: Expected log pointwise predictive density for new data; the target that WAIC and LOO estimate. Higher is better. [M4 §4.6](module4.qmd#t4-6)

Empirical Bayes
: Estimate the hyperparameters from the data, then plug them in as known. Ignores their uncertainty. [M5 §5.3](module5.qmd#t5-3)

Equivalent sample size
: How many observations a prior is "worth"; a + b − 2 for Beta(a, b) in the notes' convention. [M2 §2.7](module2.qmd#t2-7)

Estimand
: The quantity that answers the research question, often computed from parameters draw by draw. [M4 §4.11](module4.qmd#t4-11) · [Project step 1](project.qmd#p1)

Gamma–Poisson
: Conjugate pair for rates: Gamma(α, β) prior, Poisson counts with exposure E, posterior Gamma(α + y, β + E). [M2 §2.10](module2.qmd#t2-10)

Generative model
: A model that can simulate new data from parameters; required for posterior predictive distributions. [M1 §1.6](module1.qmd#t1-6)

Gibbs sampler
: MCMC that samples each parameter from its full conditional distribution in turn. [M3 §3.5](module3.qmd#t3-5)

GLMM
: Generalised linear mixed model: a GLM with group-level (random) effects. [M5 §5.7](module5.qmd#t5-7)

Grid approximation
: Evaluating prior × likelihood on a grid and normalising by the sum. Works for one or two parameters. [M1 §1.4](module1.qmd#t1-4) · [M2 §2.1](module2.qmd#t2-1)

Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC)
: MCMC that uses the gradient of the log posterior to make long, well-aimed proposals. [M3 §3.7](module3.qmd#t3-7)

HPD interval
: Highest posterior density interval: the shortest region containing the stated probability. [M1 §1.5](module1.qmd#t1-5)

Hyperprior / hyperparameter
: The prior on the parameters of the group-level distribution (e.g. μ and τ). [M5 §5.3](module5.qmd#t5-3)

Improper prior
: A "prior" that does not integrate to 1, e.g. flat on the real line. May or may not give a proper posterior. [M2 §2.4](module2.qmd#t2-4)

Jeffreys' prior
: $p(\theta) \propto \sqrt{I(\theta)}$; invariant under reparameterisation. [M6 §6.7](module6.qmd#t6-7)

Kullback–Leibler divergence
: $\int g \log(g/f)$: a non-negative, asymmetric measure of how far a predictive distribution f is from the true g. [M4 §4.6](module4.qmd#t4-6)

## L–P

Likelihood
: $p(y \mid \theta)$ as a function of θ for fixed data. [M1](module1.qmd#t1-4)

linpred / epred / predict
: brms functions giving draws of the linear predictor, the expected outcome, and a new observation. [M3 §3.12](module3.qmd#t3-12)

LKJ prior
: Prior for correlation matrices of varying effects; `lkj(2)` mildly favours correlations near 0. [M5 §5.8](module5.qmd#t5-8)

LOO-CV / PSIS-LOO
: Leave-one-out cross-validation, approximated from one fit by Pareto-smoothed importance sampling. [M4 §4.8](module4.qmd#t4-8)

loo_compare
: Ranks models by elpd; reports each model's difference from the best and the SE of the difference. [M4 §4.9](module4.qmd#t4-9)

MAP
: Maximum a posteriori: the posterior mode. [M1 §1.5](module1.qmd#t1-5)

Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)
: Algorithms that generate a dependent sequence of draws whose distribution converges to the posterior. [M3 §3.4](module3.qmd#t3-4)

Median odds ratio (MOR)
: $\exp(0.954\,\tau)$ for a logistic GLMM: the median odds ratio between two random groups. [Project step 1](project.qmd#p1)

Metropolis(–Hastings)
: MCMC that proposes a move and accepts it with probability min(1, posterior ratio), corrected for asymmetric proposals in MH. [M3 §3.6](module3.qmd#t3-6)

Monte Carlo standard error (MCSE)
: The simulation error of an MCMC or Monte Carlo estimate; about posterior SD / √ESS for a mean. [M3 §3.2](module3.qmd#t3-2) · [§3.10](module3.qmd#t3-10)

No pooling
: Each group estimated from its own data only. [M5 §5.2](module5.qmd#t5-2)

NUTS
: No-U-Turn Sampler: HMC that chooses its path length automatically; Stan's default. [M3 §3.7](module3.qmd#t3-7)

Pareto k̂
: Diagnostic per observation in PSIS-LOO; values above 0.7 make the approximation unreliable. [M4 §4.8](module4.qmd#t4-8)

Partial pooling
: Group estimates shrunk towards the population mean by an amount learned from the data; the hierarchical model. [M5 §5.2](module5.qmd#t5-2)

Posterior predictive check (PPC)
: Comparing replicated data from the fitted model with the observed data. [M4 §4.2](module4.qmd#t4-2)

Posterior predictive distribution
: The distribution of new data after integrating over the posterior. [M1 §1.6](module1.qmd#t1-6)

Posterior predictive p-value
: $P(T(y^\text{rep}) \geq T(y) \mid y)$; near 0 or 1 signals misfit for statistic T. [M4 §4.3](module4.qmd#t4-3)

Precision
: 1 / variance. In the normal–normal model, precisions add. [M2 §2.2](module2.qmd#t2-2)

Prior predictive check
: Simulating data from the prior alone to see what the prior implies; `sample_prior = "only"` in brms. [M6 §6.2](module6.qmd#t6-2)

## R–Z

R-hat (Gelman–Rubin)
: Ratio of total to within-chain variability; ≈ 1 when chains agree. The notes use < 1.1, current Stan advice < 1.01. [M3 §3.9](module3.qmd#t3-9)

Reference prior
: A prior chosen to maximise the data's influence (expected KL divergence from prior to posterior). [M6 §6.7](module6.qmd#t6-7)

Rejection sampling
: Draw from a proposal and accept with probability f/(c·g); exact but inefficient in many dimensions. [M3 §3.3](module3.qmd#t3-3)

Sensitivity analysis (prior)
: Refitting with alternative priors to see whether conclusions change. [M6 §6.5](module6.qmd#t6-5)

Sequential updating
: Using the posterior from one dataset as the prior for the next; gives the same result as one combined analysis. [M2 §2.5](module2.qmd#t2-5)

Shrinkage
: Pulling an estimate towards a prior or population mean, more for noisier estimates. [M2 §2.3](module2.qmd#t2-3) · [M5 §5.4](module5.qmd#t5-4)

Simulation-based calibration (SBC)
: Checking that posterior quantiles of true values drawn from the prior are uniform. [M6 §6.6](module6.qmd#t6-6)

Stacking
: Weighting models' predictive distributions to maximise LOO predictive performance of the mixture. [M4 §4.10](module4.qmd#t4-10)

Student-t likelihood
: Heavy-tailed alternative to the normal, robust to outliers; `family = student()`. [M4 §4.5](module4.qmd#t4-5)

Temporal coherence
: Specifying the prior before seeing the data and not revising it; broken whenever the data guide model changes. [M6 §6.3](module6.qmd#t6-3)

Test statistic T(y)
: A summary of the data used in a posterior predictive check. [M4 §4.3](module4.qmd#t4-3)

Thinning
: Keeping every k-th draw. Lowers autocorrelation but discards information; rarely useful with NUTS. [M3 §3.10](module3.qmd#t3-10)

Trace plot
: Parameter value against iteration, one line per chain. [M3 §3.8](module3.qmd#t3-8)

Varying slopes
: Group-specific slopes (and usually intercepts) with a covariance matrix: `(1 + x | group)`. [M5 §5.8](module5.qmd#t5-8)

WAIC
: Widely applicable information criterion: −2 × (lppd − p_WAIC), fully pointwise and Bayesian. [M4 §4.7](module4.qmd#t4-7)

Weakly informative prior
: A prior that rules out absurd values but otherwise lets the data speak. [M6 §6.4](module6.qmd#t6-4)

:::
